title: Normalized ordinary-etale Tate-power presentation and comparison
statement: Use the finite coefficient setting $P$ of [def-pur-conventions]. Put $A=P.\mathrm{Coefficient}$ and $N=P.\mathrm{diagonalExponent}$, and let $T$ be a scheme with $N$ invertible in $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. Write $D_d=P.\mathrm{diagonalTwistEtale}(T,d)$ for the ordered $d$-fold derived tensor of the shifted root line, with $D_0=A_T[0]$ [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Let $B_d$ be the ordinary etale Tate sheaf $A_T(d)$ of [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist], with $B_0=A_T$, and put $S_d=B_d[0]$. All tensor products below are the ordinary etale sheaf tensor or its derived functor [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Define $\mathrm{EtalePowerPresentation}(P,T)$ to consist of isomorphisms $e_d:D_d\xrightarrow{\sim}S_d[2d]$ for every $d\geq0$, with the following prescribed normalization. At zero $e_0$ is the inverse zero-shift unitor. For each $d$, $e_{d+1}$ is the composite of (i) $e_d$ tensored on the right with the shifted root line, (ii) the specified tensor-shift comparison moving shifts $2d$ and $2$ outside tensor, (iii) the flat single-complex tensor comparison for $B_d$ and $B_1$, (iv) the single-complex image of the sheaf-power step $B_d\otimes B_1\simeq B_{d+1}$, and (v) the shift identification $2d+2=2(d+1)$ used in [def-pur-frame-class]. The sheaf-power step is the left tensor unitor at $d=0$ and the identity of the recursively defined tensor power thereafter. Flatness is that of these locally free rank-one sheaves [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Endpoint presentations in this prescription are identified with the actual displayed tensor and shift comparisons, not arbitrary isomorphisms. Define $\mathrm{etalePowerComparison}(P,T,d)$ as the comparison component of the uniquely normalized presentation. Also name the sheaf-power product, its zero unitor and step, the single-complex object $S_d$, and the etale derived tensor used in this construction. This is precisely the existing ordered-power construction, not a choice of an unnormalized Tate-line isomorphism.
